evidence: Clear package/module structure based on business domains (e.g., control/bot, control/weather, control/calendar) with dedicated modules per data source/service
Low average fan-out (1.15) and shallow directory depth (max 4) indicate cohesive, minimally coupled modules
Centralized entry points (main.py, run.py) orchestrate modules without heavy inter-module dependencies
No network-based service communication; all interaction is via direct Python imports and function calls
Shared utilities (utils/*) and domain-specific control modules (control/*) follow modular monolith conventions
Tests mirror module structure (tests/test_control, tests/test_db), suggesting localized responsibility
Use of scheduling (APScheduler) and event-driven微信 handling fits a single-process, cohesive application
risks: Moderate risk of increasing coupling due to direct cross-module imports observed (e.g., data_collection → control modules)
No runtime isolation between modules — failure in one can impact entire application
Limited scalability if more services/features are added without architectural refactoring
